title: Headcount
context: HR needs the current employee headcount for a board slide.
task: How many employees are listed in the Employees table?
hint: Count the entries in the column that holds employee names — they are text, so a plain number count won't work.

title: Monthly payroll
context: Finance wants the total monthly salary bill for all staff.
task: What is the combined monthly salary across every employee?
hint: Find the column that holds each person's salary and total it.

title: Average salary
context: A dashboard shows the typical monthly salary as a whole number.
task: What is the average monthly salary across all employees, shown with no decimal places?
hint: Average the salary column, then wrap it so it reports to zero decimals.

title: Highest salary
context: Compensation wants to know the top of the pay scale.
task: What is the highest monthly salary paid to any employee?
hint: Look for the largest value in the salary column.

title: Earliest hire
context: HR wants the hire date of the longest-serving employee.
task: What is the earliest hire date in the Employees table?
hint: Dates are stored as numbers, so the earliest is the smallest value in the hire-date column.

title: Engineers
context: The Engineering lead wants their team's headcount.
task: How many employees work in the Engineering department?
hint: Count the rows whose department equals Engineering.

title: Active employees
context: Reporting should exclude staff who have resigned.
task: How many employees currently have a status of Active?
hint: Count the rows whose status equals Active.

title: High earners
context: HR wants to know how many staff sit above the six-figure mark.
task: How many employees earn more than 100,000 per month?
hint: Count salaries using a greater-than criterion.

title: Sales payroll
context: The Sales director wants the department's salary bill.
task: What is the total monthly salary of everyone in the Sales department?
hint: Sum salaries, but only for rows where the department is Sales.

title: Remote payroll
context: Finance is costing out the fully remote workforce.
task: What is the total monthly salary of employees based Remote?
hint: Sum salaries where the location is Remote.

title: Average G3 salary
context: HR wants the typical pay for grade G3 staff.
task: What is the average monthly salary of employees at grade G3?
hint: Average salaries, filtered to rows where the grade is G3.

title: Annual salary
context: Salaries are stored monthly, but an offer letter needs the yearly figure.
task: What is the annual salary of the employee in row 2?
hint: Scale that person's monthly salary up to a full year.

title: Bonus amount
context: Each employee's bonus percentage is stored as a whole number (e.g. 12 means 12%).
task: What is the monthly bonus amount for the employee in row 2, in currency?
hint: Apply the person's bonus percentage to their salary — remember the percentage is written as a whole number.

title: Total comp
context: Total compensation is salary plus the bonus it earns.
task: What is the total monthly compensation (salary plus bonus) for the employee in row 3?
hint: Grow the salary by its bonus percentage — the percentage is a whole number, so mind the parentheses.

title: Senior flag
context: Grades G4 and G5 are considered senior.
task: Label the employee in row 2 as "Senior" if their grade is G4 or G5, otherwise "Staff".
hint: An IF whose test allows either of two grades to pass.

title: Above average?
context: HR flags whether a person earns more than the company average.
task: For the employee in row 2, return "Above" if their salary beats the average salary, otherwise "Below".
hint: Compare that person's salary against the average of the whole salary column inside an IF.

title: Clean a name
context: The name in row 9 was imported with stray spaces and inconsistent capitalisation.
task: Return the employee name in row 9 with extra spaces removed and in proper case.
hint: Two nested text functions: one strips extra spaces, one fixes the capitalisation.

title: Employee email
context: Company emails follow first.last@datahub.io, all lower case.
task: Build the datahub.io email address for the employee in row 2 from their name.
hint: Swap the space in the name for a dot, force lower case, then attach the domain by joining text.

title: First name
context: A mail-merge greeting needs just the first name.
task: Extract the first name (the text before the first space) from the employee name in row 2.
hint: Find the position of the space, then take the characters to its left.

title: Employee code
context: Internal codes are the first three letters of the department in capitals, followed by the employee ID.
task: Build the employee code for row 2 (e.g. Marketing 1001 becomes MAR1001).
hint: Take the first three department letters in upper case and join the employee ID onto them.

title: Hire year
context: Finance groups tenure reporting by joining year.
task: In which year was the employee in row 2 hired?
hint: Extract the year from the hire date.

title: Tenure in years
context: HR wants completed years of service as of today.
task: How many full years has the employee in row 2 worked here, as of today?
hint: Measure the whole years between the hire date and today's date.

title: Probation end
context: Probation runs for six months from the hire date.
task: On what date does probation end for the employee in row 2 (six months after hire)?
hint: Shift the hire date forward by a set number of months.

title: Total leave taken
context: The Leave table logs one row per leave request with the number of days.
task: How many leave days have been logged in total across all requests?
hint: Total the column in the Leave table that holds days per request.

title: Sick leave requests
context: HR tracks how often sick leave is used.
task: How many leave requests were of type Sick?
hint: Count the leave rows whose type equals Sick.

title: Earned leave days
context: HR wants total days taken as Earned leave.
task: How many days of Earned leave have been taken in total?
hint: Sum the days column, but only for rows where the leave type is Earned.

title: Grade minimum
context: The Grades table maps each grade to its salary band.
task: Look up the minimum salary of the pay band for the grade of the employee in row 2.
hint: Match the employee's grade into the Grades table and pull back the band's minimum-salary column.

title: Grade bonus rate
context: The Grades table lists the standard bonus rate for each grade.
task: Look up the standard bonus percentage for the grade of the employee in row 2.
hint: Match the grade into the Grades table; work out which column holds the bonus rate.

title: Salary range
context: Compensation wants the spread between the highest- and lowest-paid staff.
task: What is the difference between the highest and lowest monthly salary?
hint: Subtract the smallest salary from the largest.

title: Remote engineer?
context: A flag identifies remote members of the Engineering team.
task: For the employee in row 2, return TRUE only if they are based Remote AND work in Engineering.
hint: Combine two conditions that must both hold.

title: Needs review
context: HR flags anyone who has resigned or is paid below the floor of 40,000.
task: For the employee in row 2, return TRUE if they have Resigned OR earn less than 40,000.
hint: Either condition being true is enough.

title: Missing locations
context: A data-quality check looks for employees with no location recorded.
task: How many employees are missing a Location value?
hint: Count the blank cells in the location column.

title: Share of payroll
context: HR wants to see how much of the total payroll one person accounts for.
task: What fraction of the total monthly payroll does the employee in row 2 represent?
hint: Divide that person's salary by the total of all salaries.

title: Salary in thousands
context: A summary shows salaries in thousands (K) to one decimal place.
task: Express the salary of the employee in row 2 in thousands, to one decimal place.
hint: Scale the salary down by a thousand and round to one decimal.
